scope: Single-sheet schematics generated from a pinned intended circuit. Keep component references, values, and electrical connectivity unchanged while improving presentation.

criteria.requirement: Every required component reference and value is legible and clearly associated with its own symbol.

measurements.source: schematic review engine default maximum field-envelope distance
independent native symbol-anchor and text-envelope observer

visual_rubric: Read each reference and value on the full-page image or its supplied detail image; flag fields that are too small, clipped, visually stranded, or ambiguous despite passing distance checks.
Confirm each field is visually closest and clearly related to its owning symbol, not a neighboring symbol.
criteria.limitation: The 25.4 mm locality limit and non-overlap checks catch specific geometric defects; they do not establish human legibility or association by themselves. The 5.08 mm owner-advantage heuristic catches gross geometric mismatches; it does not prove human association.

criteria.requirement: The page has balanced functional grouping, clear reading flow, and enough space to follow the circuit without crowding.
visual_rubric: Inspect the full page for recognizable functional groups and a natural signal-flow direction.
Flag excessive unused space, crowding, fragmented motifs, confusing crossings, or a page that requires zooming to understand the main organization.
Use the detail image to confirm that local labels, pins, wires, and branches remain easy to follow.
criteria.limitation: The 65% utilization value is a starting layout target, not a validated human-quality threshold; balance and flow remain visual judgments pending P6-011b qualification.

criteria.requirement: Where local REF/VCC routing is feasible, show continuous visible wires from the relevant terminals to a shared rail instead of relying only on repeated same-name labels.

measurements.source: independent native netlist comparison to the pinned intended circuit
independent native wire-geometry path between asserted-net terminals

visual_rubric: For each REF or VCC net present in the intended circuit, trace the visible line from each local power terminal or flag to the common wire trunk; flag label-only joins or apparent gaps.
Check that branch junctions are visibly unambiguous and do not visually merge distinct supply or return nets.
If an obstacle or page constraint prevents a visible route, report that specific obstacle and treat the criterion as unresolved rather than silently accepting label-only connectivity.
criteria.limitation: Netlist equivalence proves electrical identity, not visible wire continuity. The visual rubric is not yet qualified, and applicability for complex or multi-sheet power domains is outside this brief. The wire-path gate proves explicit conductor geometry between asserted-net terminals; image review still judges whether the trunk and branches are easy to follow.
